body:
### Problem

On macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 26.5), several `nvim --embed` server processes were left orphaned (PPID 1, reparented to launchd) after their builtin-TUI parents exited. Each orphan consumed ~100% of one CPU core continuously (observed for days, until killed).

`sample` of the stuck processes consistently shows:

```
getout
└─ os_exit
   └─ event_teardown
      └─ loop_close
         └─ uv_walk
            ├─ loop_walk_cb
            └─ uv_is_closing
```

i.e. the process is stuck inside the `uv_walk()` force-close fallback in `loop_close()` (`src/nvim/event/loop.c`).

The existing 2-second teardown timeout in `loop_close()` is ineffective in this state: it is only checked **after** `uv_walk()` returns, and `uv_walk()` never returns when the libuv `handle_queue` is cyclic/corrupted. The timeout was added precisely to guarantee a bounded exit (#11821, #11820), but this code path bypasses it.

A minimal C reproducer shows that a cyclic `handle_queue` makes `uv_walk()` spin at ~100% CPU forever, matching the observed stack signature exactly:

```c
#include <uv.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

static void walk_cb(uv_handle_t *h, void *arg) {
  if (!uv_is_closing(h)) uv_close(h, NULL);
}
static void noop(uv_timer_t *h) {}
int main(void) {
  uv_loop_t loop; uv_loop_init(&loop);
  uv_timer_t t[3];
  for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    uv_timer_init(&loop, &t[i]);
    uv_timer_start(&t[i], noop, 100000, 0);
  }
  // Fault injection: make the intrusive handle queue cyclic (models the
  // corrupted state observed in the stuck processes).
  t[1].handle_queue.next = t[0].handle_queue.next;
  t[1].handle_queue.prev = t[0].handle_queue.prev;
  uv_walk(&loop, walk_cb, NULL);  // never returns, ~100% CPU
  return 0;
}
```

Fixing libuv's `uv_walk()` itself is not viable: with an already-corrupted intrusive linked list there is no safe recovery, and even a bounded walk can still crash afterwards. The defense belongs in Nvim's exit path: do not call `uv_walk()` (which force-closes unknown luv handles anyway), keep `UV_RUN_NOWAIT`, and let the existing timeout fire so the process always exits, logging the remaining handles via `log_uv_handles()`.

A local patch removing the `uv_walk()` fallback from `loop_close()` builds cleanly, passes `make lintc`, the startup/exit functional tests, and the TUI `:detach` tests on current master. Trade-off: a plugin that leaks an active libuv handle now costs ~2s + exit code 1 with a logged handle list, instead of being silently force-closed.

I was unable to determine how the `handle_queue` becomes cyclic through supported Nvim API usage (see below), so this report intentionally covers the hang + timeout bypass; the underlying corruption source is still unknown.

### Steps to reproduce

The actual trigger is **not reproducible on demand**. Evidence from the real occurrences:

- Five independent `nvim --embed` orphans across different projects/sessions, all with the same `loop_close → uv_walk` spin stack.
- Each held different resources (0–12 unix sockets, 0–22 swap files, 5 kqueues), so no single plugin/resource type is common to all.
- stdio fds 0/1/2 were kernel-revoked; the parent TUI PIDs were gone.
- Hundreds of stress attempts did **not** reproduce the queue corruption: `--clean` and full-config `:qall!`, killing the TUI parent with SIGKILL/SIGHUP/SIGTERM, rapid pty teardown, hundreds of timers/signals/FSEvents watchers, many buffers+swap files, Snacks explorer, LSP, and GC churn.

The C reproducer above demonstrates the spin mechanism and is provided as the smallest faithful model; it is not the corruption source.

### Expected behavior

The exit path must be bounded even when a handle cannot be closed:

- `loop_close()` should never depend on `uv_walk()` returning; the existing 2s timeout must always be reachable.
- On timeout, log remaining handles (`log_uv_handles()`) and exit.

Consider dropping the `uv_walk()` force-close fallback entirely (it also cannot run resource-specific close callbacks, per the existing `XXX` comment), or bounding it so teardown always terminates.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.12.4
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1785763465

Current master (`e8a1addb5`, v0.13.0-dev-1307) still contains the same `loop_close()` structure (verified by source inspection); the hang was not reproduced on master.

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

n/a (not a Vim issue; relates to Nvim's `loop_close()`/libuv teardown)

### Operating system/version

macOS 26.5, Apple Silicon (arm64)

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty 1.3.1

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty

### Installation

Homebrew (`neovim` 0.12.4, `libuv` 1.52.1, `luv` 1.52.1-0)

Related: #25575 (macOS hang inside `loop_close` at a different point — `uv__fsevents_close` semaphore wait; closed without repro).
title: loop_close() spins at 100% CPU inside uv_walk() (cyclic libuv handle queue); 2s teardown timeout bypassed
